free_tier.stated: Reserve an upload slot with `POST /channels/{id}/attachments` and PUT the body straight into Discord's Google Cloud Storage bucket. The reservation path accepts up to 500 MiB per file, independent of the 20 MiB message-time limit. Note the file still hits the per-message limit when you actually send it, so 500 MiB only helps if the channel/boost tier allows it.

record.tooling: Documented unofficial-API reference (docs.discord.food, formerly 'userdoccers'); Python pseudocode in the page; used in production by large bots. No dedicated library needed. Two HTTP calls.
record.chaining: Upload slots are per-channel, so the 500 MiB ceiling multiplies by channel count (500/server) rather than by account.
record.limits_note: 1-10 files per reservation call; `is_clip` flag grants a 100 MiB default; requires same permissions as normal attach; `DELETE /attachments/{upload_filename}` to clean up unused reservations.
record.reliability_note: Endpoints are undocumented-but-stable and have moved URL shape before; a reservation you do not consume needs explicit deletion or it lingers.

evidence.proved: 'This allows you to upload up a file up to 500 MiB directly to Google Cloud. Note that file size limits will still apply when sending the attachment in a message.'
'When uploading a clip, an increased default file size limit of 100 MiB applies.'
